iso-27001.name: ISO 27001
fixes: Write a one-page scope statement and get leadership to sign it off.
Name an accountable executive and document security roles.
Adopt a risk method (likelihood × impact) and build a risk register.
Map all 93 Annex A controls, justify inclusions and exclusions.
Publish a policy set and track staff acknowledgement.
Run onboarding training plus quarterly phishing simulations.
Write an incident playbook and run a tabletop exercise.
Schedule an independent internal audit, then a management review.

iso-42001.name: ISO 42001 · AI governance
fixes: Inventory the AI you build, buy and use, then write a scope statement leadership signs off.
Publish an AI policy and name who approves, owns and monitors each AI system.
Adopt an AI risk method and record the risks of each AI system in a register.
Make an AI system impact assessment a gate before deployment.
Map the 38 Annex A controls and justify inclusions and exclusions.
Record provenance, quality checks and usage rights for training and input data.
Set acceptable-use rules for AI tools and add AI terms to supplier due diligence.
Track performance and incidents per AI system, then run an internal audit and management review.

nist-csf.name: NIST CSF 2.0
fixes: Agree a risk appetite with leadership and report cyber risk alongside other business risks.
Name an accountable executive and document who decides, who does and who checks.
Tier suppliers by risk and add security requirements to contracts and onboarding.
Build an asset inventory and give every critical asset an owner.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for admins first, then everyone.
Set patch deadlines by severity and prove backups with a scheduled restore test.
Centralise logs and alerts for critical systems and define who responds to them.
Write response and recovery playbooks and run a tabletop exercise.

ransomware.name: Ransomware & incident readiness
fixes: Keep at least one backup copy offline or immutable and restore from it on a schedule.
Close any remote access without MFA, starting with admin and VPN accounts.
Track internet-facing assets and patch known-exploited vulnerabilities first.
Deploy EDR on all endpoints and servers and assign who watches the alerts.
Send key logs to one place and keep them for at least 90 days.
Write a short plan naming who leads, who decides and who to call, including outside help.
Run a two-hour tabletop with leadership, including the pay or don't-pay decision.
List deadlines and contacts for regulators, your insurer, law enforcement and customers.
